Date: 2028-05-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Samantha Ortiz (Everleaf Head of AI), Devon Park (Everleaf Infra Lead), Liam O'Connor (Everleaf PM)
Notes: Renewal conversation + additional EU/APAC region activation and latency/resilience planning.
summary: Light renewal check-in where Everleaf signaled intent to extend for another year if EU region activation and latency fallbacks are validated. Discussed tradeoffs between Dedicated reserved capacity vs Hosted with burst and VPC/onprem options for sensitive ad-serving workloads. Agreement to run a focused benchmark and exchange SOC2+KMS docs before pricing finalization.
topics: Renewal timing and contract extension options
EU region activation and data residency
Latency SLOs / fallback policies and dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs
Benchmark plan and success criteria for pilot
transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time, really appreciate it, um we wanted to do a quick renewal and region activation sync — keep it tight.
[00:07] Samantha Ortiz: yeah thanks Alyssa, we've got about 30 minutes, Devon's gonna jump in on infra.
[00:12] Devon Park: hey all, morning from Dublin, quick heads up we have two blockers: EU data residency confirmation and a predictable latency envelope for our live ranking service.
[00:22] Marco Ruiz: got it, thanks Devon. we brought some ideas around dedicated pools + fallback routing and how that compares to hosted with reserved burst.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: our timeline is quarter-end — we want region active and low-latency for the seasonal campaign in July, so contract needs to be signed by mid May ideally.
[00:40] Alyssa Chen: okay mid-May sign is tight but doable. Question for Sam/Devon: are you set on VPC/private deploy for EU or would a Redwood-hosted EU region with encryption at rest and KMS suffice?
[00:52] Samantha Ortiz: preference is hosted EU with strict residency, but legal wants KMS and the audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. On-prem would be more friction.
[01:03] Devon Park: yes, if you can provide KMS-integration and cross-account logging, hosted is fine; we just need deterministic failover so we don't spike latency during peak.
[01:12] Marco Ruiz: that's something Redwood's routing can do — can set regional primary to eu-west and fallback to us-east with model-variant mapping so the quality drop is controlled. There is a cost/latency tradeoff though.
[01:25] Samantha Ortiz: walk us through the numbers — particularly token cost and p99 latency impact if we route to US as fallback.
[01:33] Alyssa Chen: sure, rough ballpark: hosted eu region with reserved capacity gives you flat monthly cost but lower cross-region tail latency; burst on demand saves upfront but p99 may double during fallback because of extra hop.
[01:46] Liam O'Connor: are there options to run lightweight quantized model in EU and full model in dedicated US pool? hybrids maybe?
[01:55] Marco Ruiz: exactly — we've done hybrid setups: quantized 4-bit proximate model for 90% of traffic, with routing to higher-accuracy variants for long-form inference. It reduces per-token cost and keeps tail latency acceptable for most requests.
[02:10] Devon Park: sounds promising — what about KV cache warmup and prefix caching? our ranking calls are chatty and we see cache churn.
[02:18] Marco Ruiz: auto-prefix caching and sticky sessions help. our serving runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache eviction policies tuned per workload. We'll show you a benchmark for your access pattern.
[02:30] Samantha Ortiz: can you include our sample logs? we can provide a 24-hour sample trace.
[02:35] Alyssa Chen: yes please send the trace — Marco will build the plan.
[02:39] Samantha Ortiz: one more question — SOC2 plus ISO? our procurement asked for both and KMS HSM notes.
[02:45] Alyssa Chen: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 documentation, and we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS/HSM integrations. We'll attach the certs and a short KMS hookup doc.
[02:57] Liam O'Connor: awesome. On pricing: what's the minimum commit for dedicated to justify the latency SLO?
[03:03] Marco Ruiz: depends on throughput. For your forecast (peak 1.2M tokens/day) we recommend a small dedicated pool — roughly 4 GPUs reserved — which lowers per-token cost by about 28% versus full hosted burst at peak. We'll put numbers in the workbook.
[03:17] Devon Park: is there a non-disruptive canary/rollout path? we can't have a big cutover risk.
[03:22] Marco Ruiz: yes, rollout supports canary traffic by route; you can pin model versions and we have automatic fallback policies with health checks — if the dedicated pool degrades, requests route to hosted variants.
[03:33] Samantha Ortiz: great — and do you expose tracing hooks? our observability team needs per-route traces and token-level cost.
[03:39] Alyssa Chen: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token breakdowns, and traces you can pipe to your APM; we also support exporting audit logs to your S3 or SIEM.
[03:49] Liam O'Connor: quick objection from procurement: how do you compare to NimbusAI? they're offering lower baseline but limited regional options.
[03:55] Alyssa Chen: Nimbus's base price may look lower, but they saddle you with unpredictable tail cost and less mature fallbacks. Redwood's differentiator is predictable economics + routing and observability which translates to lower ops cost and less incident time.
[04:10] Samantha Ortiz: understood. ok what's next steps — we need a benchmark run and then price + PO.
[04:16] Marco Ruiz: Proposed benchmark: 1-hour run using your 24-hour trace, measure p50/p90/p99 latency, token cost, and error rates across eu-west and us-east routes. We'll test hybrid quantized vs full models.
[04:28] Devon Park: timeline: can you run this next week? we can spin up test VPC and share creds.
[04:33] Marco Ruiz: yes, target next Tue or Wed. I'll send a schedule link after this call.
[04:38] Alyssa Chen: I'll send the reserved capacity worksheet and an initial proposal by Friday, include two options: hosted-eu reserved and small dedicated pool with canary.
[04:46] Samantha Ortiz: ok if we get the benchmark and the SOC docs soon, we can sign mid-May.
[04:50] Alyssa Chen: perfect — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[04:54] Liam O'Connor: thanks, bye.
[04:55] (call ends)
